name: Zeus
description: King of gods and men
notes: src:theoi-zeus|src:homer-iliad|src:ovid-metamorphoses|src:hesiod-theogony
column14: Youngest child of Cronus and Rhea. Ruler of Mount Olympus. Known for numerous affairs with goddesses and mortal women.

name: Hera
description: Queen of gods and goddess of marriage and family
notes: Wife of Zeus. Protector of married women. Known for jealousy of Zeus's lovers. Queen of heaven.

name: Poseidon
description: God of the sea earthquakes and horses
notes: Brother of Zeus. Known as the earth-shaker. Created the horse and caused earthquakes.

name: Demeter
description: Goddess of agriculture grain and harvest
notes: Sister of Zeus. Mother of Persephone. Caused the first winter when her daughter was abducted.

name: Athena
description: Goddess of wisdom warfare strategy and crafts
notes: Daughter of Zeus born from his head. Patron of Athens. Known for strategic warfare and wisdom.

name: Apollo
description: God of the sun music prophecy and healing
notes: Son of Zeus and Leto. God of the sun with a golden chariot. Gave prophecies at Delphi.

name: Artemis
description: Goddess of the hunt moon and virginity
notes: Daughter of Zeus and Leto. Twin sister of Apollo. Goddess of the hunt and protector of young women.

name: Ares
description: God of war violence and bloodlust
notes: Son of Zeus and Hera. Represents brutal aspects of war contrasting with Athena's strategic warfare.

name: Hephaestus
description: God of fire metalworking and crafts
notes: Son of Zeus and Hera (or Hera alone). Blacksmith of the gods. Threw out of Olympus; settled in Lemnos.

name: Aphrodite
description: Goddess of love beauty and sexuality
notes: Goddess of love and beauty. Born from sea foam. Married to Hephaestus but lover of Ares.

name: Hermes
description: God of messengers travelers merchants and thieves
notes: Son of Zeus and Maia. Known as Thoth in Egyptian traditions. Guide of souls to the underworld.

name: Dionysus
description: God of wine ecstasy theater and fertility
notes: Son of Zeus and mortal Semele. Only male Olympian god born of a mortal woman. God of wine and ecstasy.

name: Hestia
description: Goddess of the hearth home and family
notes: Eldest child of Cronus and Rhea. Goddess of the hearth. Chose peace over conflict; allowed Dionysus to take her seat.

name: Kronos
description: King of the Titans god of agriculture and wealth
notes: Son of Uranus and Gaia. Overthrown by Zeus. Imprisoned in Tartarus. Associated with golden age of mankind.

name: Hades
description: God of the underworld the dead and wealth
notes: Brother of Zeus and Poseidon. Ruler of the Underworld. Married to Persephone. Known as wealth god (valuable minerals).

name: Persephone
description: Goddess of spring vegetation and the underworld
notes: Daughter of Demeter. Abducted by Hades. Spends half year in underworld; half on earth (explaining seasons).

name: Rhea
description: Titaness and mother of the Olympian gods
notes: Titaness daughter of Uranus and Gaia. Mother of the twelve Olympians. Associated with mother earth and fertility.

name: Ouranos
description: Primordial god of the sky and heavens
notes: Primordial Titan. Father of the Titans. Castrated by Kronos. Associated with night sky and cosmic order.

name: Gaia
description: Primordial goddess of the earth and nature
notes: Primordial goddess of the earth. Mother of the Titans. Represents the physical earth and nature itself.

name: Tethys
description: Titaness of fresh water and mother of river gods
notes: Titaness daughter of Uranus and Gaia. Wife of Oceanus. Mother of the Oceanids and river gods. Goddess of fresh waters.

name: Oceanus
description: Titan god of the ocean and water
notes: Titan god of the ocean. Father of the Oceanids. Unlike Poseidon represents the oceanic waters themselves.

name: Iapetus
description: Titan god of mortality and the west
notes: Titan son of Uranus and Gaia. Father of Prometheus Epimetheus and Atlas. Associated with mortal death.

name: Themis
description: Titaness of divine justice and law
notes: Titaness of divine justice. Mother of the Fates and Seasons. Gave prophecies before Apollo at Delphi.

name: Mnemosyne
description: Titaness of memory and mother of the muses
notes: Titaness daughter of Uranus and Gaia. Slept with Zeus for nine nights bearing the nine Muses. Goddess of memory.

name: Coeus
description: Titan god of intelligence and knowledge
notes: Titan son of Uranus and Gaia. Associated with intelligence and the axis of heaven. Father of Leto.

name: Phoebe
description: Titaness of bright intellect and moon
notes: Titaness of bright intellect. Gave the gift of prophecy to Apollo. Grandmother of Apollo and Artemis.

name: Hyperion
description: Titan god of light and the sun
notes: Titan son of Uranus and Gaia. Father of Helios Selene and Eos. Associated with divine light.

name: Helios
description: Titan god of the sun
notes: Titan god of the sun. Rides golden chariot across sky daily. Later merged with Apollo. Witnessed all mortal deeds.

name: Selene
description: Titan goddess of the moon
notes: Titan goddess of the moon. Rides silver chariot across night sky. Fell in love with mortal Endymion.

name: Eos
description: Titan goddess of the dawn
notes: Titan goddess of the dawn. Announces the sun's arrival daily. Mother of the winds and stars. Lover of mortal Tithonus.

name: Theia
description: Titaness of light and brightness
notes: Titaness of divine radiance and light. Mother of Helios Selene and Eos. Personifies golden radiance.

name: Eros
description: God of love desire and sexual passion
notes: God of love. Appears as winged youth with bow and arrows. Son of Aphrodite (or Chaos and Night). Causes desire in gods and mortals.

name: Nike
description: Goddess of victory and success
notes: Goddess of victory. Attendant of Zeus. Wings represent swift victory. Associated with athletic competitions.

name: Athena Nike
description: Variant of Athena emphasizing victory
notes: Athena in her role as bringer of victory. Distinct cult at Athens particularly regarding military victory.

name: Tyche
description: Goddess of fortune fate and chance
notes: Goddess of chance and good fortune. Later associated with the prosperity of cities. Personifies randomness and luck.

name: Iris
description: Goddess of the rainbow and messenger of gods
notes: Goddess and messenger of the gods especially of Hera. Personifies the rainbow. Serves as mediator between divine and mortal realms.

name: Hebe
description: Goddess of youth and rejuvenation
notes: Daughter of Zeus and Hera. Cupbearer of the gods. Made Heracles immortal by giving him youth and vitality.

name: Eris
description: Goddess of chaos discord and strife
notes: Goddess of discord. Threw golden apple causing Trojan War. Embodies rivalry and conflict among mortals.

name: Nemesis
description: Goddess of retribution and justice
notes: Goddess of retribution and divine justice. Punishes hubris and excessive pride. Maintains cosmic balance.

name: Moirai
description: Goddesses of fate and destiny (Clotho Lachesis Atropos)
notes: Three goddesses controlling human destiny. Clotho spins thread. Lachesis measures it. Atropos cuts it. Even Zeus respects their power.

name: Horai
description: Goddesses of the seasons and natural order
notes: Three goddesses representing order and seasons. Daughters of Themis. Guard the gates of Olympus and Underworld.

name: Nyx
description: Primordial goddess of night and darkness
notes: Primordial goddess of night. Mother of Sleep Dreams and Strife. Even Zeus feared to anger her.

name: Hypnos
description: God of sleep and slumber
notes: God of sleep. Lives in cave beneath earth. Brother of Death. Can put anyone to sleep including gods.

name: Morpheus
description: God of dreams and sleep
notes: God of dreams. Son of Hypnos (Sleep). Brings dreams to mortals. Shapes dreams with great skill.

name: Thanatos
description: God of peaceful death
notes: God of death. Brings peaceful death to mortals when their time comes. Twin of Sleep (Hypnos).

name: Erinyes
description: Goddesses of vengeance and punishment
notes: Three fearsome goddesses who punish oath-breakers murderers and the impious. Born from blood of Uranus.

name: Hephaestus Servants
description: Servants and creations of Hephaestus
notes: Magical beings created by Hephaestus including Talos and bronze servants of the gods.

name: Pan
description: God of shepherds flocks forests and wild places
notes: God of shepherds and wild nature. Half-goat half-human. Plays panpipes. Associated with panic and fear in wilderness.

name: Satyrs
description: Demigods of the forest and wild revelry
notes: Companions of Dionysus. Half-human half-animal creatures. Associated with wine music and wild nature.

name: Naiads
description: Nymphs of fresh water sources
notes: Nymphs of streams springs and rivers. Daughters of Oceanus or Tethys. Known for their beauty and mischievous nature.

name: Dryads
description: Nymphs of the forests and trees
notes: Nymphs of trees and forests. Each dryad is connected to a specific tree. Represent nature's vitality and protection.

name: Nereids
description: Nymphs of the sea and ocean
notes: Fifty sea nymphs daughters of Nereus. Associated with serenity and protection of sailors. Live in Aegean Sea.

name: Nereus
aliases: Old Man of the Sea, Néreus
description: Ancient sea god and father of the Nereids
notes: Ancient sea god. Can transform into any shape. Known for truthfulness and wisdom. Father of fifty Nereids.

name: Oceanus & Tethys
description: Titan deities of water and fresh water
notes: Primordial Titan couple representing oceanic and fresh waters respectively.

name: Amphitrite
aliases: Queen of the Sea, Tethys variant
description: Queen of the sea and wife of Poseidon
notes: Queen of the sea wife of Poseidon. Mother of Triton. Commands sea creatures and protects sailors.

name: Triton
description: Messenger of the sea and son of Poseidon
notes: Son of Poseidon and Amphitrite. Part-human part-fish. Messenger of the sea. Calms or stirred up waves.

name: Asclepius
description: God of medicine and healing
notes: Son of Apollo. God of medicine and healing. Known for bringing dead back to life (angered Zeus).

name: Hecate
description: Goddess of witchcraft crossroads and magic
notes: Goddess of witchcraft and magic. Guards crossroads. Guides travelers and protects households. Commands ghosts and demons.

name: Styx
description: Goddess of oaths and the river in Underworld
notes: Titaness of the river Styx in Underworld. Oaths sworn on her waters are binding even to gods.

name: Heracles
description: Greatest hero of antiquity known for twelve labors
notes: Son of Zeus and mortal Alcmene. Greatest hero of Greek mythology. Completed twelve seemingly impossible labors for king Eurystheus.

name: Perseus
description: Hero who slew Medusa and saved Andromeda
notes: Son of Zeus and Danae. Slew Medusa using her reflection in his polished shield. Rescued Andromeda and married her.

name: Theseus
description: King of Athens hero of multiple adventures
notes: Son of Poseidon or Aegeus. King of Athens. Slew Minotaur. Went on many adventures including journey to Trojan War.

name: Jason
description: Leader of the Argonauts on quest for Golden Fleece
notes: Leader of the Argonauts. Sailed on Argo seeking Golden Fleece. Married and loved Medea (who later betrayed him).

name: Andromeda
description: Princess of Ethiopia rescued by Perseus
notes: Ethiopian princess sacrificed to sea monster Cetus. Rescued by Perseus with whom she had many children. Mother of Perseid dynasty.

name: Medea
description: Sorceress who helped Jason and later betrayed him
notes: Daughter of Helios and Oceanid. Powerful sorceress. Helped Jason win Golden Fleece but later killed their children in revenge.

name: Achilles
description: Greatest Greek warrior of Trojan War
notes: Son of Nereid Thetis and mortal Peleus. Invincible Greek warrior. Slew Hector. Died at Troy killed by Paris's arrow to heel.

name: Hector
description: Prince of Troy and greatest Trojan warrior
notes: Prince of Troy. Greatest Trojan warrior. Killed by Achilles. Son of Priam and Hecuba. Dragged behind Achilles' chariot.

name: Ajax
description: Great Greek warrior second only to Achilles
notes: Son of Telamon. Strongest Greek after Achilles. Fought heroically at Troy. Later driven mad and committed suicide over arms of Achilles.

name: Agamemnon
description: High king of Greece and leader of Greeks at Troy
notes: King of Mycenae and leader of Greek forces at Troy. Known for pride and arrogance. Murdered by his wife Clytemnestra.

name: Menelaus
description: King of Sparta and cause of Trojan War
notes: King of Sparta. Husband of Helen whose elopement with Paris caused Trojan War. Fought at Troy for ten years.

name: Helen
description: Most beautiful woman in ancient world spark of Trojan War
notes: Daughter of Zeus and Leda. Wife of Menelaus. Her elopement with Trojan prince Paris sparked Trojan War. Symbol of beauty and desire.

name: Paris
description: Trojan prince whose judgment led to Trojan War
notes: Son of King Priam of Troy. Judgment of beauty contest started Trojan War. Killed Achilles. Died at Troy.

name: Odysseus
description: Resourceful Greek hero of the odyssey
notes: Son of Laertes or Sisyphus. Greek hero at Troy. Took 10 years to sail home to Ithaca. Known for cunning intelligence.

name: Ajax the Lesser
description: Greek warrior from Locris
notes: Son of Oileus. Smaller less famous Ajax. Committed sacrilege in Athena's temple at Troy. Drowned by Athena in revenge.

name: Patroclus
description: Close companion of Achilles
notes: Companion and close friend of Achilles. Borrowed Achilles' armor and died in battle. His death drove Achilles to fury.

name: Diomedes
description: Greek warrior known for valor at Troy
notes: Son of Ares or Tydeus. Brave Greek warrior at Troy. Wounded Aphrodite and Ares in battle. Journeyed extensively after Troy.

name: Aeneas
description: Trojan hero who founded Rome
notes: Son of Aphrodite and Trojan hero. Escaped burning Troy carrying father on his back. Sailed to Italy founding Rome.

name: Priam
description: King of Troy at time of Trojan War
notes: King of Troy during Trojan War. Father of Hector Paris and many other children. Killed by Achilles' son Neoptolemus.

name: Hecuba
description: Queen of Troy wife of Priam
notes: Queen of Troy. Wife of Priam. Mother of Hector and Paris. After Troy's fall transformed into a dog (in some versions).

name: Andromache
description: Wife of Hector and mother of Astyanax
notes: Wife of Hector. Mother of Astyanax. After Troy's fall enslaved and given to Achilles' son Neoptolemus.

name: Atalanta
description: Swift-footed huntress
notes: Swift huntress participant in Argonaut expedition. Competed in foot races. Could not be beaten until suitor used golden apples to slow her.

name: Ariadne
description: Princess who helped Theseus escape Labyrinth
notes: Daughter of King Minos. Helped Theseus navigate Labyrinth by giving him ball of string. Later married Dionysus.

name: Orestes
description: Greek hero who avenged his father
notes: Son of Agamemnon. Avenged father by killing mother Clytemnestra. Pursued by Furies. Represented justice through revenge.

name: Electra
description: Daughter of Agamemnon devoted to avenging father
notes: Daughter of Agamemnon and Clytemnestra. Devoted to avenging father's murder. Helped her brother Orestes get revenge.

name: Cassandra
description: Prophetess cursed never to be believed
notes: Daughter of Priam. Cursed by Apollo to prophesy truth but never be believed. Tried to warn of Trojan Horse. Killed after Troy's fall.

name: Medusa
description: Once-beautiful woman turned into monstrous gorgon

name: Once-beautiful woman. Cursed by Athena for affair with Poseidon. Transformed into gorgon with snakes for hair. Killed by Perseus.
Hippolytus
description: Son of Theseus cursed by Aphrodite
notes: Son of Theseus and Amazon queen. Cursed by Aphrodite for rejecting her. Falsely accused and killed tragically.

name: Minotaur
description: Half-man half-bull creature
notes: Half-man half-bull monstrosity. Kept in Labyrinth at Crete. Offspring of Pasiphae and sacred bull. Killed by Theseus.

name: Hydra
description: Multi-headed serpent with regenerating heads
notes: Monstrous serpent with multiple heads. Killing one head caused two to grow back. Defeated by Heracles.

name: Chimera
description: Multi-headed fire-breathing creature

name: Monstrous creature with lion goat and serpent parts. Fire-breathing. Killed by hero Bellerophon.
Cerberus
description: Three-headed guard dog of Hades

name: Three-headed guard dog of Underworld. Guards entry to Hades' realm. One of Heracles' Twelve Labors to capture him.
Pegasus
description: Winged horse divine steed
notes: Divine winged horse born from Medusa's neck. Immortal. Carries heroes into battle. Later placed in sky as constellation.

name: Python
description: Serpent slain by Apollo
notes: Giant serpent or dragon. Guarded Oracle at Delphi. Slain by Apollo in one of his first great deeds. Later oracles conducted on site.

name: Mount Olympus
description: Highest mountain of Greece home of the Olympian gods
notes: Highest mountain in Greece (2918m). Home of the 12 Olympian gods. Divine palace with eternal spring weather.

name: Underworld
description: Realm of the dead ruled by Hades
notes: Dark realm below earth ruled by Hades. Divided into Elysium (blessed souls) Tartarus (evil souls) and Asphodel (average souls).

name: Troy
description: Ancient city in Asia Minor seat of Trojan War
notes: Ancient city in what is now Turkey. Site of the Trojan War. Besieged for 10 years by Greeks. Destroyed and rebuilt many times.

name: Delphi
description: Site of Apollo's oracle the center of Greek world
notes: Ancient sanctuary and oracle of Apollo. Considered center of ancient Greek world (omphalos). Source of prophecies for centuries.

name: Labyrinth
description: Elaborate maze on Crete housing the Minotaur

name: Elaborate maze built by Daedalus to house Minotaur. Located on Crete. Theseus navigated it with Ariadne's thread.
Tartarus
description: Deepest part of Underworld where titans imprisoned
notes: Deepest part of Underworld. Imprisoned Titans after their defeat. Contains worst punishments for wicked souls.

name: Elysium
description: Paradise in Underworld for blessed souls
notes: Blessed region of Underworld for virtuous and heroic souls. Eternal paradise with perfect weather and beauty.

name: Athens
description: Capital city of Greece patronized by Athena
notes: Capital of Greece. Patronized by Athena. Center of art philosophy and democracy. Home to famous temples including Parthenon.

name: Sparta
description: Military city-state of Greece ruled by Menelaus
notes: City-state in ancient Greece. Known for military prowess. Ruled by Menelaus. Rival to Athens in ancient Greece.

name: Crete
description: Large island home of King Minos and Labyrinth
notes: Large Mediterranean island. Home of King Minos and Labyrinth. Advanced Minoan civilization. Center of mythology.

name: Ithaca
description: Small island home of Odysseus
notes: Small rocky island in Ionian Sea. Home of Odysseus. Hero spent 10 years trying to return there from Troy.

name: Corinth
description: Ancient Greek city-state
notes: Ancient Greek city-state. Important trading hub. Ruled by various kings. Known for walls and harbors.
